body:
Query with
```py
func.array_remove(table.c.options, Options.OPTION1)
```
will give the same error

Hi,

array of enum is a bit troublesome, we have had s number of other issues all related to casts.

Does using `sa.cast(Options.OPTION1, Enum(Options))` work?

Yes it does.
I've dug sources a little and reduced example to
```python
import enum
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, MetaData, Table, Column, Enum
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import ARRAY, dialect

class Options(enum.Enum):
    OPTION1 = '1'
    OPTION2 = '2'
    OPTION3 = '3'

table = Table(
    'bug', MetaData(),
    Column('options', ARRAY(Enum(Options))),
)
d = dialect()

q = table.select().where(table.c.options.contains([Options.OPTION1]))
print(q.compile(dialect=d).bind_names)

q = table.select().where(table.c.options.any(Options.OPTION1))
print(q.compile(dialect=d).bind_names)
```

Following patch fixes this specific issue with `any()` (tested on b2ab2bbf4faf508b3fa5749969019203a702786f)
```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/sqltypes.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/sqltypes.py
index 4f8654a..a4ba8e5 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/sqltypes.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/sqltypes.py
@@ -2809,7 +2809,7 @@ class ARRAY(SchemaEventTarget, Indexable, Concatenable, TypeEngine):
             # send plain BinaryExpression so that negate remains at None,
             # leading to NOT expr for negation.
             return elements.BinaryExpression(
-                coercions.expect(roles.ExpressionElementRole, other),
+                coercions.expect(roles.ExpressionElementRole, other, type_=self.type.item_type),
                 elements.CollectionAggregate._create_any(self.expr),
                 operator,
             )
```
but I'm not sure if it is a good idea as a whole

looking at the codepath used by contains() i think this is the most appropriate approach, short of replacing the construction of the BinaryExpression here with "self.operate()":

```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/sqltypes.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/sqltypes.py
index 4f8654afd9..3d97decf8b 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/sqltypes.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/sqltypes.py
@@ -2809,7 +2809,12 @@ class ARRAY(SchemaEventTarget, Indexable, Concatenable, TypeEngine):
             # send plain BinaryExpression so that negate remains at None,
             # leading to NOT expr for negation.
             return elements.BinaryExpression(
-                coercions.expect(roles.ExpressionElementRole, other),
+                coercions.expect(
+                    roles.BinaryElementRole,
+                    element=other,
+                    operator=operator,
+                    expr=self.expr,
+                ),
                 elements.CollectionAggregate._create_any(self.expr),
                 operator,
             )
@@ -2849,7 +2854,12 @@ class ARRAY(SchemaEventTarget, Indexable, Concatenable, TypeEngine):
             # send plain BinaryExpression so that negate remains at None,
             # leading to NOT expr for negation.
             return elements.BinaryExpression(
-                coercions.expect(roles.ExpressionElementRole, other),
+                coercions.expect(
+                    roles.BinaryElementRole,
+                    element=other,
+                    operator=operator,
+                    expr=self.expr,
+                ),
                 elements.CollectionAggregate._create_all(self.expr),
                 operator,
             )
```
ok the above patch is how I think we shoudl do this if someone wants to add some tests and push up a patch.
and the patch doesnt work in main, so , back to the drawing board

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**properly type array element in any() / all()** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/3808

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_4** branch:

**properly type array element in any() / all()** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/3809

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

I can't use an enum type as part of a `case()` without casting.

Looks very similar to https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/6515

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.36

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

psycopg2

### Database Vendor and Major Version

PostgreSQL 12

### Python Version

3.11

### Operating system

macOS

### To Reproduce

```python
import enum

from sqlalchemy import case, create_engine, update, types as sqltypes
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, sessionmaker

Session = sessionmaker()


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class State(enum.Enum):
    PENDING = enum.auto()
    RUNNING = enum.auto()
    CANCELLING = enum.auto()
    CANCELLED = enum.auto()
    
    
StateType = sqltypes.Enum(State)


class Job(Base):
    __tablename__ = "jobs"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    state: Mapped[State] = mapped_column(StateType, server_default=State.PENDING.name)


def main(engine):
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(
            update(Job).values(
                state=case(
                    (
                        Job.state == State.PENDING,
                        State.CANCELLED,
                    ),
                    else_=State.CANCELLING,
                )
            )
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    engine = create_engine("postgresql:///issue12097", echo=True)
    Session.configure(bind=engine)
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
    try:
        main(engine)
    finally:
        Base.metadata.drop_all(engine)
```


### Error

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1967, in _exec_single_context
    self.dialect.do_execute(
  File ".venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/default.py", line 941, in do_execute
    cursor.execute(statement, parameters)
psycopg2.ProgrammingError: can't adapt type 'State'

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "issue12096.py", line 50, in <module>
    main(engine)
  File "issue12096.py", line 32, in main
    conn.execute(
  File ".venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1418, in execute
    return meth(
           ^^^^^
  File ".venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/sql/elements.py", line 515, in _execute_on_connection
    return connection._execute_clauseelement(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1640, in _execute_clauseelement
    ret = self._execute_context(
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1846, in _execute_context
    return self._exec_single_context(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1986, in _exec_single_context
    self._handle_dbapi_exception(
  File ".venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 2355, in _handle_dbapi_exception
    raise sqlalchemy_exception.with_traceback(exc_info[2]) from e
  File ".venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1967, in _exec_single_context
    self.dialect.do_execute(
  File ".venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/default.py", line 941, in do_execute
    cursor.execute(statement, parameters)
sqlalchemy.exc.ProgrammingError: (psycopg2.ProgrammingError) can't adapt type 'State'
[SQL: UPDATE jobs SET state=CASE WHEN (jobs.state = %(state_1)s) THEN %(param_1)s ELSE %(param_2)s END]
[parameters: {'state_1': 'PENDING', 'param_1': <State.CANCELLED: 4>, 'param_2': <State.CANCELLING: 3>}]
(Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/20/f405)
``` 

It works if I add casts:
```python
            update(Job).values(
                state=case(
                    (
                        Job.state == cast(State.PENDING, StateType),
                        cast(State.CANCELLED, StateType),
                    ),
                    else_=cast(State.CANCELLING, StateType),
                )
            )
```

### Additional context

mcve requires you to run `createdb issue12097` first.

### Describe the bug

array of enum can't be used with any_/all_()

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

current

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

pg

### Database Vendor and Major Version

pg

### Python Version

current

### Operating system

any

### To Reproduce

```python
import enum

from sqlalchemy import ARRAY
from sqlalchemy import Column
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy import Enum
from sqlalchemy import MetaData
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy import Table

m = MetaData()


class MyEnum(enum.Enum):
    ONE = enum.auto()
    TWO = enum.auto()
    THREE = enum.auto()

t = Table("t", m, Column("data", ARRAY(Enum(MyEnum))))


e = create_engine("postgresql://scott:tiger@localhost/test", echo=True)
m.drop_all(e)
m.create_all(e)


with e.connect() as conn:

    # fine
    expr = t.c.data.any(MyEnum.TWO)
    conn.execute(
        select(t).where(expr)
    )

    # t.c.data.any_() coerces to boolean and fails for left side.
    # this seems to not happen for strings though
    expr = MyEnum.TWO == t.c.data.any_()
    conn.execute(
        select(t).where(expr)
    )
```
